subject.title: improve(sqlite): harden state lifecycle and snapshots

question: Should state backup fail closed when a plugin-owned SQLite database cannot be compact-snapshotted with the capabilities available to core?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but this is an intentional operator-visible compatibility choice: it prevents deleted-page exposure while causing backups that previously included raw plugin database files to stop and require plugin-owner capability support.

options.title: Accept fail-closed backups
options.body: Keep the strict compact-snapshot requirement and require affected plugin owners to provide compatible SQLite capabilities or a future owner-defined snapshot contract.

options.title: Define plugin snapshot API first
options.body: Pause the strict plugin-database behavior until an explicit plugin snapshot and verification capability exists.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed backups
recommendation.body: Keep the strict compact-snapshot requirement and require affected plugin owners to provide compatible SQLite capabilities or a future owner-defined snapshot contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history owns the database-first state, backup, and transcript architecture whose compatibility policy this PR extends.
